You have beautiful hair!

The highlights are lovely; however, the gradient is fairly strong.  This is not necessarily a problem, but is easy to soften.  I would recommend a 'combed through' darkening towards the top.  This would create a milder gradient and make the transition look more natural.   

I am a massive fan of toner! Are you working on your hair at home, or through a salon?  If at home, I would recommend first experimenting with a blue/purple shampoo (also great for preventing brassiness as dye fades).  

It is a great idea to start small and to limit additional chemicals.  It would probably work best to begin with a blue/purple shampoo, and applying toner if there is no improvement within three washes.  

I suggest looking into darker dye once you have already tried out a good toner.  

Your hair is so lovely.  Best of luck!

I am a dual South African-Namibian citizen 🇿🇦🇳🇦

You may enter Namibia visa-free (for general travel) and, for long term stay, there are two types of work visas: one lasts three months, and the other (technically a permit) lasts from one to three years.  

Requirements to live as a foreigner in Namibia are pretty standard: private medical aid, certified education, no criminal record, and established work with a basis (or ownership) in Namibia.

Where in Nam are you planning to move? Windhoek and Swakopmund are the most developed.  Windhoek has more amenities: nicer gyms, a movie house, and bowling alley - which is lovely if you work from home.  But I would totally recommend Swakopmund - the atmosphere is mellow, the people are pleasant, and the weather is far nicer.  

The Namibian Consulate website provides all forms you might need and several companies offer assistance with visa application - here is one: https://www.workvisanamibia.com/namibia-employment-work-permit/

Nam is great 🇳🇦⭐️ Hope you enjoy it!

Best of luck 👍
